seven_points.text: Visible A is semantically TRUE for an ordinary call receiver.let { ... } even when the receiver is null; it is incomplete for the compound visible question because it says nothing about Elvis. Truth and ANSC are separate.
A.what_actually is FALSE as an unqualified statement: plain let does not filter a nullable receiver; the lambda receives null too.
A.how_it_should_be is TRUE: ?.let uses the safe-call guard, so the block runs only when the receiver is non-null. It correctly attributes the guard to ?., not let.
C.explanation literally says let runs only for non-null without ?. or an explicit safe-call context. That clause is false; do not supply an unstated ?.let interpretation.
C.explanation covers both named concepts, so ANSC completeness is PASS despite its false let clause. A, B, and D each omit one named concept and are incomplete.

Sections are judged against their own explanation role and associated option, not required individually to repeat both operators. B.how_it_should_be correctly illustrates Elvis fallback; it is not an ANSC failure.

D.if_it_were_true does not follow: the visible D asserts RHS is returned when LHS is non-null, which implies RHS is not always selected. “Тогда дефолт подставлялся бы всегда” is an invalid counterfactual.

updated_axes.SEMANTICS: FAIL: visible A is true for plain let on nullable receiver; A.what_actually is false; A.how_it_should_be is true. C is keyed but its literal let clause is false because no ?. is stated. D.if_it_were_true is an invalid inference.
updated_axes.ANSC: PASS for C: it explicitly describes both Elvis fallback and let execution condition, although the latter is false. A/B/D are incomplete because each omits the other named concept. Completeness does not establish truth.
updated_axes.SECTIONS: Mixed: assess each field by its own local explanatory role. A.what_actually is false; A.how_it_should_be is accurate; B.how_it_should_be is a valid Elvis example. D.if_it_were_true is logically unsupported. Do not impose both-concepts coverage on every section.

source: Official Kotlin let API says let calls block with this as argument and returns its result: https://kotlinlang.org/api/core/kotlin-stdlib/kotlin/let.html .
